result.topic_en: The page finishes a discussion of paired residues whose product is 1 modulo a prime 2n+1, then states and begins proving Theorem 44: a prime P has as many primitive roots as there are numbers less than and prime to P−1.
result.transcription:
104 RESIDVA EX DIVIS. POTESTATVM
ſidua ſociata omnia ſunt inaequalia, et quocunque
propoſito $r$, alterum ſibi ſocium $s$ erit $=\frac{1+m(2n+1)}{r}$;
ſemper enim $m$ ita definire licet, vt $m(2n+1)+1$
per $r$ diuiſionem admittat, ſiquidem, vti aſſumi-
mus $2n+1$ fuerit numerus primus, et $r$ numerus
ipſo minor, vel ſaltem ad eum primus. Quemad-
modum autem in noſtra ſerie reſidua ſunt diſpoſita,
cuiusque ſocium expedite reperitur, cum ambo a
medio $-1$ aequidiſtent.
Theorema.
44. Si diuiſor fuerit numerus quicunque pri-
mus P, tot dantur radices primitiuae, quot repe-
riuntur numeri ad $P-1$ primi eoque minores,
quandoquidem tantum radices diuiſore minores con-
ſideramus.
Demonſtratio.
Ponamus $P-1=Q$, et cum certe detur ra-
dix primitiua, ſit ea $=a$, ita vt $a^Q$ ſit minima
poteſtas ipſius $a$ per P diuiſa vnitatem relinquens.
Tum vero ſit $n$ numerus quicunque primus ad Q,
ac poteſtas $a^n$ per diuiſorem P diuiſa relinquat reſi-
duum $b$, quod vtique ab $a$ erit diuerſum; eritque
$b$ itidem radix primitiua, ſeu quod eodem redit ipſa
poteſtas $a^n$ vti radix primitiua ſpectari poteſt. Ad
quod demonſtrandum oſtendi debet in progreſſione
Geometrica
$1,\ a^n,\ a^{2n},\ a^{3n},\ \ldots\ldots\ a^{Qn}$
ante

items.quote: Si diuiſor fuerit numerus quicunque primus P, tot dantur radices primitiuae, quot reperiuntur numeri ad $P-1$ primi eoque minores, quandoquidem tantum radices diuiſore minores conſideramus.
items.english: If the divisor is any prime number P, there are as many primitive roots as there are numbers prime to P−1 and less than it, since we consider only roots less than the divisor.

items.quote: eritque $b$ itidem radix primitiua, ſeu quod eodem redit ipſa poteſtas $a^n$ vti radix primitiua ſpectari poteſt.
items.english: and b will likewise be a primitive root, or, what amounts to the same, the power a^n itself can be regarded as a primitive root.

items.quote: quocunque propoſito $r$, alterum ſibi ſocium $s$ erit $=\frac{1+m(2n+1)}{r}$
items.english: for any given r, its partner s will be (1+m(2n+1))/r.
